description: 59 deterministic, statically checkable rules for the live /frappe-review web tool (MVP Phase 1 + 8 rules from the Impertio-Studio/Frappe_Claude_Skill_Package review, 2026-11-27, + FR-040 corrected and 16 rules from the official frappe/skills review, 2026-11-27). No rule runs code.
name: frappe-sensei

rules.description: Form or controller logic for our own DocType lives in hooks.py or public/js instead of its own <name>.py / <name>.js.
rules.fix: Move the logic into the DocType's own controller <name>.py / form script <name>.js.
rules.pattern: File-structure check: a .py/.js file outside doctype/<name>/ contains logic (validation, set_query, button handlers) for a DocType owned by this app; hooks.py contains function bodies, not only hook mappings.
rules.title: Own DocType logic in hooks.py or public/js

rules.description: A file inside another app's directory (frappe, erpnext, hrms, crm, helpdesk) was edited instead of extending it from our app.
rules.example_good: # my_app/my_app/overrides/sales_order.py, wired via doc_events in hooks.py
rules.fix: Never edit another app's files; extend via doc_events in hooks.py plus an overrides module and fixtures.
rules.pattern: File-path check: changed file path starts with apps/frappe/, apps/erpnext/, apps/hrms/, apps/crm/ or apps/helpdesk/ and is not a vendored dependency.
rules.title: Another app's files edited directly

rules.description: Business logic for another app's DocType is written as a function body in hooks.py instead of a doc_events entry pointing at an overrides module.
rules.example_bad:
# hooks.py
doc_events = {'Sales Order': {'validate': lambda doc, m: doc.set('total', 0)}}
rules.fix: Put the logic in <app>/<module>/overrides/<name>.py and reference it from doc_events in hooks.py.
rules.pattern: AST check on hooks.py: a def at module level whose body contains validation or business logic, or a doc_events value that is an inline lambda; doc_events must map to '<app>.<module>.overrides.<name>.<function>'.
rules.title: Other app's DocType logic placed in hooks.py directly

rules.description: frm.set_query is called outside the form script's setup or onload handler, so the filter is applied at the wrong time or not at all.
rules.fix: Move frm.set_query into the setup (or onload) handler of the correct form script.
rules.pattern: JS AST check: a frm.set_query() call whose enclosing function is not named setup or onload, or a set_query call at top level of the form script.
rules.title: set_query outside setup/onload

rules.description: The same DocType has two or more frappe.ui.form.on blocks, or the same event handler is defined twice.
rules.fix: Merge the handlers into a single frappe.ui.form.on block per DocType.
rules.pattern: JS AST check: count frappe.ui.form.on('<DocType>', ...) calls per file; flag a DocType appearing more than once, or the same event key twice in one block.
rules.title: Duplicate frappe.ui.form.on blocks

rules.description: The same controller method (validate, on_submit, before_insert, and so on) is defined more than once in one DocType controller.
rules.fix: Merge the duplicate methods into one and extend the existing handler.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: count method definitions with the same name inside one class; flag any name defined twice.
rules.title: Duplicate controller methods

rules.description: A Custom Field or Property Setter for another app's DocType is created in code or edited JSON instead of being shipped as a fixture filtered by module.
rules.example_bad: # custom field created by a script and never added to fixtures
rules.example_good: # fixtures/custom_field.json, exported with a module filter, in my_app/fixtures/
rules.fix: Ship the Custom Field / Property Setter as a fixture filtered by module.
rules.pattern: File-structure check: a Custom Field / Property Setter definition for a DocType owned by another app appears outside the app's fixtures/ directory.
rules.title: Custom Field for another app not shipped as a fixture

rules.description: Errors are raised with raise Exception instead of frappe.throw, so the user gets an untranslated traceback instead of a clean message.
rules.example_bad:
if total < 0:
    raise Exception('Total cannot be negative')
rules.example_good:
if total < 0:
    frappe.throw(_('Total cannot be negative'))
rules.fix: Replace raise Exception with frappe.throw(_('...')).
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a Raise node whose exception is Exception, or raise with a plain string.
rules.title: raise Exception instead of frappe.throw

rules.description: A user-facing string in frappe.throw, frappe.msgprint or frappe.show_alert is not wrapped in _() / __().
rules.fix: Wrap every user-facing string in _() in Python or __() in JS.
rules.pattern: Python/JS AST check: a string literal passed directly to frappe.throw(), frappe.msgprint() or frappe.show_alert() without a _() / __() call wrapping it.
rules.title: Untranslated user-facing string

rules.description: A translation call contains an f-string, so the string cannot be translated and the placeholder is baked in.
rules.fix: Use _() with {0} placeholders and .format() instead of an f-string.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a JoinedStr (f-string) node inside a _() call; also _() with .format() on an f-string.
rules.title: f-string inside _()

rules.description: A print() call is left in server code instead of frappe.log_error or proper logging.
rules.fix: Remove print() and use frappe.log_error for jobs and integrations.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: any Call to the builtin print(). A '# noqa' comment on the same line suppresses the finding; that suppression applies to all rules.
rules.title: print() left in Python code

rules.description: A console.log, console.debug or alert() call is left in client code.
rules.fix: Remove console.log/alert() and use frappe.show_alert for user feedback.
rules.pattern: JS AST/regex check: console.log(), console.debug() or alert() calls in a .js file.
rules.title: console.log or alert() left in JS

rules.description: frappe.get_doc loads a whole document just to read one field, instead of frappe.db.get_value or frappe.get_cached_value.
rules.fix: Use frappe.db.get_value or frappe.get_cached_value for single fields.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: frappe.get_doc(<doctype>, <name>) followed by a plain field access (.field or ["field"]), with no other use of the document. A method call after get_doc (.set_status(), .save(), .insert(), .submit()) does not fire — that is an action on the document, not a single-field read. Creating a document does not fire: a dict first argument (creation form) means the document is being made, not read.
rules.title: get_doc used for a single field

rules.description: frappe.get_all or frappe.get_list is called with fields=['*'], fetching every column instead of only the fields needed.
rules.fix: List the fields you need explicitly in fields.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a get_all() or get_list() call whose fields argument is ['*'] or '*'.
rules.title: fields=["*"] in get_all / get_list

rules.description: A Server Script contains an import statement, which always fails in the RestrictedPython sandbox.
rules.example_bad:
# Server Script
import json
data = json.loads(doc.payload)
rules.fix: Remove the import and use the pre-loaded names (frappe.parse_json, frappe.utils.today, frappe.utils.flt).
rules.pattern: Python AST check, applied only when the input is marked as a Server Script: any Import or ImportFrom node.
rules.title: import statement in a Server Script

rules.description: A bare except: swallows every error, including programming errors, instead of handling a named exception.
rules.fix: Catch a named exception and handle or re-raise it with frappe.throw.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: an ExceptHandler node with type None (bare except:).
rules.title: Bare except clause

rules.description: Document values are used raw (float(), int() or plain arithmetic on a doc field) instead of flt, cint or getdate.
rules.fix: Wrap doc values with flt(), cint() or getdate() as appropriate.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: float()/int() calls on a doc attribute, or arithmetic on self.<field> / doc.<field> with no flt/cint/getdate wrapper in the same expression.
rules.title: Doc values used without flt / cint / getdate

rules.description: A validation or business rule is enforced only in client JS, so it can be bypassed by calling the API directly.
rules.fix: Enforce the rule on the server in validate / before_submit; keep JS for UX only.
rules.pattern: Cross-file check: a JS handler contains a validation (frappe.throw in JS, frm.set_df_property to block save, or a check that returns false) for a rule with no matching validate / before_submit / before_insert method in the DocType controller.
rules.title: Validation or business rule only in JS

rules.description: A method called from the form with frm.call() or frappe.call() has no @frappe.whitelist() decorator, so the call fails with 403.
rules.example_bad:
def get_order_total(name):
    return frappe.get_doc('Sales Order', name).grand_total
rules.fix: Add @frappe.whitelist() to the controller method and check permissions before returning data.
rules.pattern: Cross-file check: a frm.call() / frappe.call() target method name has no @frappe.whitelist() decorator on its Python definition.
rules.title: Form calls a method that is not whitelisted

rules.description: Field behaviour such as fetch_from, depends_on or mandatory is set in JS instead of in the DocType, where it belongs.
rules.fix: Set fetch_from, depends_on and mandatory in the DocType field settings, not in JS.
rules.pattern: JS AST check: frm.set_df_property() or frm.toggle_reqd() / frm.set_value() used to set mandatory, fetch_from or depends_on behaviour that a DocType field property covers.
rules.title: Field behaviour set in JS instead of the DocType

rules.description: Data that rarely changes is fetched with frappe.call in the refresh handler on every form open, instead of once in onload or via frm.doc.__onload.
rules.fix: Load rarely-changing data once in onload or frm.doc.__onload instead of calling on every refresh.
rules.pattern: JS AST check: a frappe.call() inside a refresh() handler for data that is not form-dependent; the controller has no onload() setting frm.doc.__onload.
rules.title: frappe.call in refresh for rarely-changing data

rules.description: User input is built into a SQL string with an f-string, % formatting or + concatenation instead of placeholders or frappe.qb.
rules.fix: Use %s placeholders with values passed separately, or frappe.qb.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: frappe.db.sql() whose first argument is a JoinedStr (f-string), a BinOp (+), or a % formatted string containing a variable.
rules.title: User input formatted into SQL (SQL injection)

rules.description: A @frappe.whitelist() method returns or writes data without checking permissions first.
rules.fix: Check frappe.has_permission before returning or writing data in every whitelisted method.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a standalone module-level @frappe.whitelist() function, or a whitelisted method that fetches another document by a passed-in docname or id, whose body contains no frappe.has_permission(), doc.has_permission(), check_permission() or permission-aware frappe.get_list() call before its first return or write — in the function itself or in a helper it calls, directly or transitively, in the same submission; instance methods of a DocType controller class (first argument self, inside a class inheriting from Document directly or through a *Controller base) are exempt unless they fetch another document by a passed-in docname or id; a function that only reads frappe.get_roles() and performs no database read or write is also exempt.
rules.title: Whitelisted method without a permission check

rules.description: A whitelisted method with allow_guest=True writes data or returns private data, which any anonymous visitor can then reach.
rules.fix: Remove allow_guest from any method that writes or returns private data; keep it only for truly public read-only endpoints.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True) on a function that calls a write API (insert/save/submit/delete/set_value) or returns a document field that is not marked public.
rules.title: allow_guest on a method that writes or returns private data

rules.description: ignore_permissions=True is used with no comment explaining why it is safe here.
rules.example_good:
# System-generated doc; the calling method already checked the business rule
doc.save(ignore_permissions=True)
rules.fix: Add a comment explaining why ignore_permissions is safe here, or remove it.
rules.pattern: Python AST/regex check: an ignore_permissions=True argument with no comment on the same line or the two lines above it explaining the reason.
rules.title: ignore_permissions without an explanatory comment

rules.description: An API key, password or token is hardcoded in code, a fixture, a JSON file or a Client Script instead of living in site_config or a Password field.
rules.fix: Move secrets to site_config.json with bench set-config and read them with frappe.conf.
rules.pattern: Regex/AST check: an assignment of a long literal string to a variable named api_key, password, secret, token or similar, or a literal token inside a .js file.
rules.title: Hardcoded secret in code, fixture or JS

rules.description: User-supplied content is rendered in Jinja without the |e filter, or with |safe, so raw HTML from a user can run (XSS).
rules.fix: Escape user content with |e and use |safe only on HTML your own code generated.
rules.pattern: Regex check on Jinja/print-format/web templates: {{ <variable> }} with no |e filter, or {{ <variable> | safe }} where the variable comes from user input.
rules.title: User content in Jinja without escaping, or |safe on user content

rules.description: User input is inserted into the page with .html() in JS instead of .text() or frappe.utils.escape_html().
rules.fix: Build DOM with .text() or frappe.utils.escape_html() instead of .html(user_input).
rules.pattern: JS AST/regex check: a .html(<variable>) call where the argument is a doc field or user-supplied value.
rules.title: User input inserted as HTML in JS

rules.description: frappe.db.commit() is called inside a controller, document hook or request path; the framework commits, and commits are blocked in v16 hooks.
rules.example_good: # no commit in the request path; the framework commits on success
rules.fix: Remove frappe.db.commit() from controllers, hooks and requests; it is allowed only in long background jobs and patches.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a frappe.db.commit() call inside a Document controller method, a doc_events hook function, or a whitelisted method.
rules.title: frappe.db.commit() in a controller, hook or request

rules.description: A database call runs inside a loop, so N rows cost N queries instead of one bulk fetch.
rules.example_bad:
for row in self.items:
    group = frappe.db.get_value('Item', row.item_code, 'item_group')
rules.example_good:
item_codes = [row.item_code for row in self.items]
groups = dict(frappe.get_all('Item', filters={'name': ('in', item_codes)}, fields=['name', 'item_group'], as_list=True))
rules.fix: Fetch in bulk before the loop, build a dict, then loop over the dict.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: frappe.db.get_value, frappe.get_doc, frappe.get_all, frappe.get_list or frappe.db.sql inside a For/While loop body. Skipped in demo / seed / test files (paths containing /demo/, /tests/ or /test_, or a filename containing seed), where loops insert demo data by design.
rules.title: Database call inside a loop (N+1)

rules.description: A bulk update saves documents one by one in a loop instead of using frappe.db.set_value with filters or a QB update.
rules.example_bad:
for name in names:
    doc = frappe.get_doc('Item', name)
    doc.status = 'Active'
    doc.save()
rules.fix: Use frappe.db.set_value with filters or a QB update for bulk changes, only when skipping controller validation is acceptable.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a .save() / .submit() call inside a loop that updates many documents of the same DocType. .insert() inside a loop is bulk creation (demo data, imports) and does not fire. Skipped in demo / seed / test files (paths containing /demo/, /tests/ or /test_, or a filename containing seed), where loops insert demo data by design.
rules.title: Bulk update done doc-by-doc with save()

rules.description: Rows are loaded into Python and summed or counted there instead of using SQL/QB Sum or Count.
rules.example_bad:
rows = frappe.get_all('Sales Invoice', fields=['grand_total'])
total = sum(r.grand_total for r in rows)
rules.fix: Aggregate in SQL/QB with Sum or Count instead of loading rows into Python.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: sum() or len() whose iterable is a direct frappe.get_all, frappe.get_list or frappe.db.sql call, or a variable assigned from such a call earlier in the same file; in-memory iterables such as self.get(...), self.items or a plain list do not fire.
rules.title: Aggregation done in Python instead of SQL

rules.description: Slow work such as bulk processing, bulk email or an external API call runs in a web request instead of a background job.
rules.fix: Move slow work to frappe.enqueue with a queue and timeout.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a whitelisted method or controller method that calls an external HTTP API, loops over a large set, or sends bulk email, with no frappe.enqueue() call.
rules.title: Slow work in a request without frappe.enqueue

rules.description: Rarely-changing master data (Company, settings, a master DocType) is read with get_value on every call instead of get_cached_value or cache=True.
rules.fix: Use frappe.get_cached_value or get_value with cache=True for rarely-changing masters.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: frappe.db.get_value() on a master DocType such as Company or a * Settings DocType with no cache=True, and no frappe.get_cached_value() nearby.
rules.title: Master data read without caching

rules.description: A simple list of document names is fetched with get_all and fields instead of pluck='name'.
rules.example_bad: names = [r.name for r in frappe.get_all('Item', fields=['name'])]
rules.fix: Use pluck='name' for simple lists of names.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: frappe.get_all(<doctype>, fields=['name']) whose result is used only as a list of names.
rules.title: Name-only list fetched without pluck

rules.description: Calling .save() from inside validate, before_save or on_update re-enters the same lifecycle hook, so the document saves in an endless loop.
rules.fix: Never call .save() from validate, before_save or on_update; use self.db_set() for a single field, or move the work to after_save or a background job.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a .save() call on self or doc inside the body of a validate, before_save or on_update method in a DocType controller; a flags-based recursion guard (self.flags) in the method exempts it.
rules.title: self.save() inside validate / before_save / on_update

rules.description: on_update runs after the document is already saved, so assigning self.<field> there changes the in-memory document only — the value never reaches the database.
rules.fix: Set the field in validate or before_save, or use self.db_set() in on_update.
rules.pattern: Python AST check: an assignment to self.<field> inside def on_update; assignments to self.flags.* and self.db_set(...) calls are exempt.
rules.title: Field assigned in on_update is never saved

rules.description: A controller that overrides validate() without calling super().validate() silently skips the parent class validation — ERPNext controller bases validate stock, pricing and more in the parent.
rules.fix: Call super().validate() first in every overridden validate().
rules.pattern: Python AST check: a validate() method in a DocType controller class whose body contains no super().validate() call.
rules.title: Overridden validate() without super().validate()

rules.description: Throwing inside a has_permission or permission_query_conditions hook breaks all access to the DocType, including read access for users who should be allowed in — the hook must return False to deny and True for users it does not restrict.
rules.fix: Never throw or raise in a permission hook; return False to deny and True for users the hook does not restrict.
rules.pattern: Python check, hooks.py only: a frappe.throw() call or a raise statement inside a def named has_permission or permission_query_conditions. A hook that ends with return None instead of return True is flagged by FR-040, not here.
rules.title: frappe.throw() or raise inside a permission hook

rules.description: A has_permission hook in hooks.py must end with an explicit return True for users the hook does not restrict. Frappe treats a missing return (None) as a denial, so a hook that only returns False in one branch silently locks out every other user.
rules.fix: End every has_permission hook with an explicit return True for users the hook does not restrict; return False only to deny.
rules.pattern: Python check, hooks.py only: a def named has_permission whose body contains no return True at all, or contains a bare return, or whose last statement is not a return — i.e. a code path that can fall through to None. Frappe treats None as a denial, so the hook must return True explicitly for unrestricted users.
rules.title: has_permission hook that can fall through to None

rules.description: cur_frm is undefined in list view, report and other non-form contexts, so code using it breaks outside the form.
rules.fix: Use the frm parameter passed to every form event handler instead of cur_frm.
rules.pattern: JS regex check: cur_frm used in a .js file.
rules.title: cur_frm used in client script

rules.description: eval() and exec() run arbitrary code from a string; they are blocked in the Server Script sandbox and are a code-injection risk anywhere else.
rules.fix: Parse data with frappe.parse_json or json.loads instead of eval/exec; legitimate uses in Frappe apps are near-zero.
rules.pattern: Python regex check: an eval( or exec( call in a .py file.
rules.title: eval() or exec() in Python code

rules.description: frappe.enqueue() without an explicit queue= relies on the framework default, so a long job can land on the short queue and time out, or a quick job can sit behind heavy work.
rules.fix: Always pass queue= explicitly — 'short', 'default' or 'long' — to frappe.enqueue().
rules.pattern: Python call-site check: a frappe.enqueue(...) call whose arguments contain no queue= keyword argument; multi-line calls are joined before checking.
rules.title: frappe.enqueue() without queue=

rules.description: Running a shell command from app code with os.system, os.popen, subprocess with shell=True, or frappe.utils.execute_in_shell hands a shell string to the OS. If any part of that string comes from a document, a request or a file name, it is command injection.
rules.fix: Use subprocess.run with a list of arguments and shell=False, or a framework API; never build a shell string from user or document data.
rules.pattern: Python check: os.system( or os.popen( or frappe.utils.execute_in_shell( anywhere, or a subprocess.* call whose arguments contain shell=True (multi-line calls joined before checking).
rules.title: Shell command built from app code (os.system / subprocess shell=True)

rules.description: pickle.loads, yaml.load without SafeLoader, marshal, dill and shelve rebuild Python objects from a byte stream. Data from a file, a request or a stored field can carry a crafted payload that runs code while it is being loaded.
rules.fix: Use json.loads / frappe.parse_json for data, or yaml.load with Loader=yaml.SafeLoader. Never unpickle data you did not create yourself.
rules.pattern: Python check: pickle.load(s)(, marshal.load(s)(, dill.load(s)(, shelve.open( or jsonpickle.decode( anywhere; yaml.load( only when the call does not pass SafeLoader.
rules.title: Unsafe deserialization (pickle / yaml.load / marshal / dill / shelve)

rules.description: frappe.render_template, render_jinja or jinja2.Template compiles its first argument as a Jinja template. If that argument is a document field, a request value or a formatted string instead of a literal, anyone who can write the field can run code on the server.
rules.fix: Pass a literal template path or string to render_template; render user-controlled content as data with |e, never as the template itself.
rules.pattern: Python check: a frappe.render_template( / render_template( / frappe.render_jinja( / jinja2.Template( call whose first argument is not a string literal (a variable, attribute, call or f-string). A literal first argument is safe and does not fire. Different from FR-027, which is about escaping data inside a template.
rules.title: Server-side template injection (render_template with a non-literal template)

rules.description: frappe.db.delete with no filter, with an empty dict, or with a filter variable a caller can leave empty deletes every row of the table. frappe.db.truncate always clears the whole table. A raw DELETE or TRUNCATE without a WHERE clause does the same.
rules.fix: Always pass a concrete filter to frappe.db.delete, and a WHERE clause to raw DELETE; use truncate only as a deliberate, commented full-table clear.
rules.pattern: Python check: frappe.db.delete( with a missing second argument, an empty {} filter, or a bare variable as the filter; frappe.db.truncate( anywhere; raw DELETE / TRUNCATE in frappe.db.sql with no WHERE in the statement. A comment on the line or the two lines above it (a deliberate full-table clear, e.g. log rotation) exempts the call — same comment rule as FR-025.
rules.title: Delete or truncate with no filter (whole table cleared)

rules.description: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE and add_index are DDL: the database commits the open transaction when they run, so a half-finished document save can be committed by accident. Schema changes belong in patches, not in request or lifecycle code.
rules.fix: Move schema changes into a patch (patches.txt + an execute() function) or into on_doctype_update; never run DDL from a whitelisted method or a lifecycle hook.
rules.pattern: Python check: frappe.db.sql_ddl(, frappe.db.add_index( / add_index(, frappe.db.truncate(, or a frappe.db.sql( call whose statement contains ALTER TABLE / CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX / DROP TABLE, outside a patch file (path containing /patches/) and outside a def named on_doctype_update.
rules.title: DDL in app code (sql_ddl / ALTER / CREATE / DROP / add_index / truncate)

rules.description: Writing a GL Entry, Stock Ledger Entry, Payment Ledger Entry, Bin or Serial and Batch Bundle row directly — by insert, save, set_value, delete or raw SQL — bypasses the posting logic that keeps the ledgers consistent. A deleted or hand-edited ledger row breaks every report built on it.
rules.fix: Never write ledger rows directly. Post, cancel or amend through the source document (Sales Invoice, Stock Entry, Payment Entry) and let the framework write the ledger.
rules.pattern: Python check: a write call (set_value, insert, save, submit, delete, delete_doc, new_doc, or a get_doc dict-creation form) on the same line as a quoted 'GL Entry', 'Stock Ledger Entry', 'Payment Ledger Entry', 'Bin' or 'Serial and Batch Bundle', or raw SQL with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `tabGL Entry` / `tabStock Ledger Entry` / `tabBin` etc. Reads (get_value, get_list, get_all, a get_doc field read) do not fire.
rules.title: Direct write to a ledger doctype (GL Entry / Stock Ledger / Bin / ...)

rules.description: Assigning an attribute on frappe, erpnext or hrms (or setattr on one of them) replaces framework code for the whole process. The patch silently breaks on the next framework upgrade, and it changes behaviour for every app on the site, not just this one.
rules.fix: Do not assign attributes on frappe, erpnext or hrms. Use a hook, an override module, or a wrapper function in your own app instead.
rules.pattern: Python check: an assignment whose left-hand side starts with frappe. / erpnext. / hrms. (excluding frappe.local, frappe.conf and frappe.session, which FR-059 covers), or a setattr(frappe|erpnext|hrms, ...) call. Assignments in test files and inside a unittest.mock.patch with-block are exempt.
rules.title: Monkey-patching frappe / erpnext / hrms at import time

rules.description: A job enqueued from inside a document save or a whitelisted method can run before the transaction commits, so it reads the old document — or no document at all if the save then fails.
rules.fix: Pass enqueue_after_commit=True to every frappe.enqueue() / enqueue_doc() called from a lifecycle method or a whitelisted method.
rules.pattern: Python check: a frappe.enqueue( or frappe.enqueue_doc( call inside a DocType lifecycle method or a @frappe.whitelist() function whose arguments contain no enqueue_after_commit=True (multi-line calls joined before checking). Complements FR-043, which is about the missing queue= keyword.
rules.title: frappe.enqueue() in a lifecycle or whitelisted method without enqueue_after_commit=True

rules.description: frappe.qb.get_query defaults to ignore_permissions=True, so a query built from it returns rows the current user is not allowed to see. In user-facing code that is a permission bypass.
rules.fix: Pass ignore_permissions=False to frappe.qb.get_query in user-facing code, or use frappe.get_list, which applies permissions.
rules.pattern: Python check: a frappe.qb.get_query( / qb.get_query( call whose arguments contain no ignore_permissions=False (multi-line calls joined before checking). An explicit ignore_permissions=True also fires.
rules.title: frappe.qb.get_query() without ignore_permissions=False

rules.description: The framework calls a fixed set of controller method names. A method named after_save, before_delete, on_saved, after_submit or before_load is never called — the customization looks installed and does nothing, with no warning.
rules.fix: Rename the method to a lifecycle name the framework calls (on_update, on_submit, before_insert, after_insert, on_trash, after_delete, on_cancel, on_change, autoname, onload, ...), or rename it to a plain helper name and call it from a lifecycle method. The same applies to doc_events keys in hooks.py.
rules.pattern: Python check: a def in a DocType controller class whose name is a known wrong lifecycle name (after_save, before_delete, on_saved, after_submit, before_load, on_submitted) or is within edit distance 2 of a real lifecycle name without being one; plus a doc_events key in hooks.py that is a wrong or near-miss lifecycle name. Ordinary helper methods with unrelated names do not fire.
rules.title: Misspelled lifecycle method name (after_save / before_delete / on_saved ...)

rules.description: frappe.local.request and frappe.form_dict exist only during a web request. Code in validate, on_update or a doc_events handler runs from background jobs, imports and patches too, where the request is empty — the rule silently reads nothing.
rules.fix: Read request data only in whitelisted methods and pass it in as an argument; lifecycle methods must work from the document alone.
rules.pattern: Python check: frappe.local.request / frappe.local.form_dict / frappe.local.response / frappe.local.request_ip / frappe.form_dict / frappe.request read inside a DocType lifecycle method, or frappe.form_dict / frappe.local.form_dict read inside any function that is not @frappe.whitelist()ed.
rules.title: Request state read inside a lifecycle method (frappe.local.request / form_dict)

rules.description: install_app stops the whole install when a before_install hook returns a falsy value. A helper that ends with a call returning None or False aborts the install silently, on a site that may simply not have the data the check looked for.
rules.fix: Never return a value from before_install; raise with frappe.throw if the install must stop, or return nothing at all.
rules.pattern: Python check: a return statement with a value inside a def named before_install (any .py file). A bare return does not fire. A return with a comment on the same line — an intentional, stated refusal — is exempt.
rules.title: return with a value inside before_install

rules.description: A dotted path in hooks.py or patches.txt that names a module or function the submitted code does not contain will fail at runtime — a renamed handler, a moved file, or a typo that nothing checks at install time.
rules.fix: Fix the dotted path to a module and function that exist in the app, or submit the whole app so the checker can resolve it.
rules.pattern: Cross-file check: a quoted dotted path in hooks.py, or a non-comment line in patches.txt, whose module part does not match any submitted .py file (excluding hooks.py itself) or whose final name is not a def/class in that file. Paths starting with frappe. / erpnext. / hrms. / crm. / helpdesk. are skipped (other apps are not submitted). Needs the whole submission's file list; a lone hooks.py with no other files is skipped entirely.
rules.title: Dotted path in hooks.py / patches.txt does not resolve

rules.description: hooks.py is imported once, before any site is selected. A frappe.db call, get_all, get_doc, get_installed_apps, frappe.local or frappe.conf read — or an if/for/while — at module level computes a value with the wrong site, or with no site at all, and caches it for every request after.
rules.fix: Keep hooks.py to static data only. Move per-site conditions into the handler body, or into a before_enable hook.
rules.pattern: Python check, hooks.py only: a frappe.db / get_all / get_doc / get_meta / get_hooks / get_installed_apps / frappe.conf / frappe.local / frappe.flags call on a line outside any def, or an if / for / while statement at module level (indent 0). Different from FR-001/FR-003, which cover logic in hooks.py — this is about values computed at import time.
rules.title: Database or site state read at module level in hooks.py

rules.description: A raw UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE through frappe.db.sql changes the database but not the cached document, so the next read returns stale data. set_value and save clear the cache themselves; a raw write must clear it by hand.
rules.example_bad:
def sync_status(name):
    frappe.db.sql("update `tabItem` set status='Active' where name=%s", name)
rules.fix: Call frappe.clear_document_cache(doctype, name) — or frappe.clear_cache(doctype=...) — in the same function after a raw SQL write.
rules.pattern: Python check: a frappe.db.sql( call whose statement is an UPDATE, INSERT or DELETE, inside a function whose body contains no frappe.clear_document_cache or frappe.clear_cache call. set_value / save do not fire — they clear the cache themselves.
rules.title: Raw-SQL write without clearing the document cache

rules.description: frappe.set_user changes who the rest of the request runs as. Without restoring the original user in a finally block, every line after the call — and every function it calls — runs as the wrong user. Assigning frappe.session.user directly does the same with no trace at all.
rules.example_good:
def run_as_admin():
    original = frappe.session.user
    try:
        frappe.set_user('Administrator')
        create_invoice()
    finally:
        frappe.set_user(original)
rules.fix: Restore the original user in a finally block after every set_user, or use frappe.only_for / a permission check instead of switching users.
rules.pattern: Python check: a frappe.set_user( call in a function whose body has no finally block that restores the user with another set_user( call, or an assignment to frappe.session.user. Both fire at the offending line.
rules.title: frappe.set_user() without restoration, or frappe.session.user assignment
